what_worked: Coherent narrative arc with honest limitations section and appropriate caution about extreme growth rates.
fix_next: You analyzed the wrong dataset entirely—every number references ~8,782 rows, not the frozen 1,000-row dataset required by the assignment.
verdict: Well-structured deck built on the completely wrong dataset.
factual_error_detail: Slide 1: 8,782 startups vs 1,000 actual rows; $227M Stripe revenue vs $13.5M reference; $255M total vs $15.6M. Slide 2: country counts (US 1,657) from wrong dataset. Slide 3: provider revenues all wrong (RevenueCat ~$9.8M vs $1.3M; Polar ~$1.9M vs $6.4K). Slide 7: AI 1,430 listings vs 197 reference; E-comm avg MRR $4,168 inconsistent with reference median $387/n=19. Every quantitative claim derives from a non-matching dataset.

evidence.insight: Slide 4 mean-vs-median divergence and slide 9 under-monetized traffic cohort show genuine analytical thinking, but all built on wrong data.
evidence.narrative: Clear 9-section arc from scope through infrastructure, revenue, leaders, momentum, categories, pricing, monetization signals to conclusion. Thesis of power-law concentration is coherent.
evidence.framing: Slide 2 data completeness table and slide 10 limitations are thoughtful, but the fundamental dataset is wrong—8,782 rows vs the required 1,000-row frozen dataset.
evidence.accuracy: Every single quantitative claim is wrong relative to the frozen reference dataset. 8,782 vs 1,000 rows; $227M vs $13.5M Stripe revenue; 1,430 AI listings vs 197. Not rounding—completely different dataset.
evidence.visual: Consistent navy/orange/accent palette, appropriate chart types (bar, scatter, pie), log scales used well on slides 4 and 9. Labels present. Competent but not exceptional.
evidence.ai_slop: Some consulting-style language ('go-to-market motion', 'defensible niche') but generally restrained. The bigger issue is dataset mismatch rather than AI slop.
